## Summary

The spec: on successful owner create, emit a line via the logger named `NOTIFY` containing the owner id and the memberId.

I made a minimal change to `OwnerAuditListener` (`src/main/java/.../model/OwnerAuditListener.java`), which is the existing `@PostPersist` hook that fires exactly on a successful insert and already derives `memberId`:

- Added a `NOTIFY` logger field.
- Added one line in `onCreate`: `NOTIFY.info("welcome owner id={} memberId={}", owner.getId(), memberId)`.

**Why this keeps structural impact low:** I touched a single file and a single tiny method. That class has only the one method, so `WMC_other ≈ 1`, `onCreate`'s cyclomatic complexity is 1, and just ~2 changed lines — the cost formula lands near its floor. Crucially I avoided the large `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (high surrounding complexity) and avoided touching `Owner.java`'s `@EntityListeners` (which would have added a second, high-`WMC_other` file to the multiplier). The `memberId` computed here (`MemberIds.of(owner)`) is the same value the DTO exposes at GET time, so it matches what the test reads back.

`AcceptanceTest.coreEnqueuesWelcome` and the full suite pass.
